Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
646 AM CDT Thu Aug 6 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonably hot with highs in the 90s and heat index values
  100-107F each day.
  
- An isolated late day shower can't be ruled out along the
  seabreeze in the afternoons.
  
- Slightly better rain chances expected Thursday into early next
  week for the eastern and southern parts of the region as some 
  deeper moisture flows back inland. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1105 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Ridging centered over the Southwest CONUS/Four Corners will keep 
uneventful weather over the region through the better half of next 
week at least. Heights and 850mb temperatures are still expected to 
drop into the weekend, resulting slightly lower heat stress and 
surface temperatures. Reduced subsidence and rising PWs should bring 
better rain chances during this period as well, with isolated to 
scattered showers and storms possible along the seabreeze/baybreeze 
each afternoon. Highs remain in the 90s each day with heat indices 
reaching the triple digits in the afternoon. Some patchy fog will be 
possible during the early morning hours.

03

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 636 AM CDT Thu Aug 6 2026

A mix of MVFR to IFR ceilings continues to develop and spread 
northward, impacting mainly KCLL, and briefly KSGR. These 
conditions are expected to persist through 13-14Z Thursday, before
gradually improving to VFR later this morning. A few showers and 
storms are possible near the terminals, but due to low confidence
in occurrence and coverage, only PROB30 groups were included. 
Winds will remain generally south-southeasterly with occasional 
afternoon gusts, especially at coastal terminals. Looking ahead 
to tonight,patchy fog and MVFR ceilings will be possible again, 
primarily near KCLL.

JM

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1105 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Onshore winds 10-15 knots and seas of 2-4 feet are expected 
throughout the next several days. Rain chances increase slightly 
through early next week. Chances for isolated to scattered showers 
and storms will be greatest during the late night through early 
afternoon hours for the Gulf.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
630 AM CDT Thu Aug 6 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A mainly typical summer weather pattern will prevail into the 
weekend. 

- There will be a chance for daily mainly afternoon showers or 
thunderstorms, however widespread significant rainfall is not 
expected.

- Muggy conditions will also occur with afternoon heat index 
readings between 100 and 107 degrees.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Today through Wednesday)
Issued at 1223 AM CDT Thu Aug 6 2026

Looking at a fairly typical pattern for this time of year that will 
continue into the weekend, with a surface ridge extending from off 
the southeast coast across the northern Gulf. This in turn will 
bring a moist low level flow with high humidity. 

Meanwhile, the forecast area will be on the periphery of an upper 
level ridge centered over the southwest US bringing a northeast flow 
in the mid levels. Do not see any significant disturbance moving 
over the area in the northeast flow, so any convection will be 
driven by daytime heating and initiated by sea breeze and other meso 
scale boundaries. Although widespread significant rainfall is not 
expected, some of the storms will be slow movers with torrential 
downpours that may cause some issues if they occur over urban poor 
drainage areas. 

Temperatures also look near norm as convective temperatures will be 
in the low 90s, so developing clouds and showers will help keep air 
temperatures from being extreme and also keeping afternoon max heat 
index values from 100 to 107 and below any heat hazards.

NBM is showing an increase in rain chances early next week as the 
upper level over the southwest US retreats to the west and the sub-
tropical ridge over the western Atlantic becomes more pronounced 
allowing for a deeper southerly flow and moisture along with a weak 
inverted trough feature to move in. 

07/Rua 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 627 AM CDT Thu Aug 6 2026

Only a few showers and a weak thunderstorm are ongoing at this 
hour near ARA and LFT. Expecting an increase in shower and 
thunderstorm activity near these terminals this morning as the 
diurnal cycle begins with sunrise. Elsewhere, activity will be 
more closely contained to the typical early afternoon seabreeze 
activity with lingering showers into sundown. 

Winds will start out variable, becoming southerly through the
morning and increasing slightly in the afternoon. The prevailing
wind should range in the 5 to 9 knot range during afternoon and
evening before decreasing again with sundown. 

11/Calhoun

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1223 AM CDT Thu Aug 6 2026

With surface high pressure ridging across the northern Gulf, winds 
will remain mainly light to modest from the southeast with low seas 
into the weekend. There will be a daily chance for showers and 
thunderstorms with the best chance closer to shore during the 
afternoon hours.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1223 AM CDT Thu Aug 6 2026

Typical hot and humid summer conditions can be expected into the 
weekend. Hit or miss showers and thunderstorms will be possible 
mainly in the afternoon. Widespread significant rainfall is not 
expected and this will likely allow the overall antecedent 
conditions to become drier with an increase in the KBDI. With low 
level Gulf moisture from mainly southerly winds, minimum afternoon 
relative humidity values are expected to range from 50 to 60 percent.
